en: The *Buddhōṣṇīṣavimalaprabhā-sarvadvārānupraveśa-sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-parīkṣā-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Volume One.
Translated at the Palace of Śakra in the Kingdom of Uḍḍiyāna, North India.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Temple, the Dharma Master Śramaṇa Śīlagupta, a subject who was conferred the purple robe, by imperial decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace.

He was joined by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, along with their retinues and the hosts of devas, including Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and the foremost sons of the gods, all of whom had gathered together.
At that time, the World-Honored One taught the Dharma based on the six pāramitās.
That is to say: regarding the dāna-pāramitā, through the fruit of giving, one obtains a great mass of merit and virtue.
They attain the mastery of non-retrogression;
the heavens rain down the seven treasures which they obtain without seeking,
and great hidden treasuries spontaneously appear.
He speaks of the *śīlapāramitā*,
namely the fruit of pure precepts:
attaining the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*) and being born in the Brahma heavens.
He speaks of the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).
That is to say, as the fruit of patience, one attains the physical marks of a celestial being,
which are exquisitely adorned and pleasing for all to behold.
He speaks of the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā),
which means that he desires to cultivate diligence so that even Māra,
the King of Demons, shall be subdued upon seeing him.
The retribution thus obtained transcends birth and death;
in an instant, one wanders through and enjoys the Buddha-fields,
expounding the dhyāna-pāramitā.
That is to say, as the fruit of pure meditative concentration, one attains the śūraṅgama-samādhi,
and further attains countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of samādhis.
He speaks of the Prajñāpāramitā;
that is to say, through the fruit of wisdom,
one attains a great mass of merit and acquires vast erudition as expansive as the ocean.
At that time, having heard this Dharma of the six pāramitās,
the assembly of devas rejoiced greatly in their hearts and contemplated, practiced, and investigated it day and night.
At that moment, there was a son of the Trāyastriṃśa gods named Maṇigarbha-vimala.
Accompanied by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of devaputras and eighteen thousand celestial maidens,
together with celestial palaces and the miraculous transformations of supernatural powers,
adorned with the seven treasures and sublime, lofty pavilions.
With various palaces and various gardens,
ponds, flowers, and fruits all exquisitely adorned,
that stainless son of heaven, Maṇigarbha, [dwelt there].
Together with the goddess Mṛdukusumā,
they take great delight in one another, following each other in walking and sitting as they experience celestial pleasures within the palace of the seven jewels, which has four gates.
Intoxicated by and deeply attached to the pleasures of the five desires,
he displayed his pride and allowed himself to fall into sleep.
At that time, the celestial son Maṇigarbha-vimala—
Even during the middle watch of the night, amidst sleep and dreams,
all the celestial maidens played exquisite music;
at that time, the yakṣa Jvālāmukha in that palace raised his voice.
He exhorted the devaputra Maṇigarbha-vimala, saying to him:
"Maṇigarbha-vimala, why do you take pleasure in your palace and indulge in the attachment of sleep?"
Without any awakening, they remain settled therein.
O Deva, you should know that your happiness will not last long;
in seven days from now, your life will certainly be impermanent.
Although the celestial joys and the palaces of the seven treasures are exquisite and beyond compare, when your life comes to an end, not even a moment can be retained.
This matter is true; you should reflect upon it yourself and quickly employ skillful means.
When the yakṣa Agnijihva had spoken these words, he suddenly vanished.
At that time, the devaputra Maṇigarbha-vimala,
having heard these words, was deeply afflicted with mental anguish.
He fell down as if intoxicated and unconscious,
his face pressed to the ground, lying prostrate and rigid.
When the host of celestial maidens saw this, they...
They were all filled with sorrow and grief, weeping and shedding tears like rain;
they were terrified and panicked, afflicted by a thousand kinds of suffering.
Furthermore, they saw that the hair of those gods was disheveled and matted.
His robes, necklaces, and all ornaments for adorning the body were cast aside to one side;
his face was stained with blood, and his lips and mouth were parched and withered.
Twofold more sorrowful and distressed, they cried out, "Alas, what suffering!
Their hearts were scorched as by fire;
they fainted and fell to the ground, and some became so bewildered that they lost their minds.
There were also those who, like fish that have lost their water, writhed upon the ground;
they uttered various sighs of grief and lamentation, crying out to heaven.
Among them, there were some who did not lose their minds.
They filled celestial jewel vessels with fresh,
cool water and sprinkled sandalwood powder over his body;
or else they combed his hair into a topknot, adjusted his robes, or supported his feet.
At that time, the Devaputra Maṇigarbha-vimala gradually regained his senses.
Having regained consciousness, after a long while, he cried out with great suffering and extreme distress: "Alas, what misery!"
He sighed deeply with long exhalations,
his body trembling and quivering like grass swaying unsteadily in the wind;
only when his voice became faint did he finally give rise to resolve.
"I shall now go swiftly to the abode of Śakra Devendra.
Having arrived there, I shall prostrate at the feet of Śakra and speak these words:
'Lord of Devas, save me! Lord of Devas, save me!'"
Having heard the words of the yakṣa Śrutolkamukha regarding the matters mentioned above, he thought:
"I shall certainly meet my end in seven days;
I contemplate the agonizing torments of the hells."
For this reason, they came in haste to inform the Lord of Devas:
"By what skillful means may we obtain liberation,
so that we do not die and fall into the evil realms?"
"O Lord of Devas, please act as our protector and deliver us from the suffering of death.
Having spoken thus,
Śakra, the Lord of Devas, heard these words.
Knowing his mind was filled with distress, he addressed the devaputra Maṇigarbha-vimala, saying:
"Do not fear, Maṇigarbha-vimala!
There has appeared in the world a Buddha, a World-Honored One, a Teacher of gods and humans, a Supreme Being."
Yet there exists a Dharma-medicine capable of saving one from birth, old age, sickness, death, and afflictions;
it causes one to distance oneself from the hells and all other evil destinies, and brings them to destruction.
Just as those parents were able to rescue you, so do I now tell you:
the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One is in the Tuṣita Palace; you must go there with all haste.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
together with the celestial son Maṇigarbha-vimala and countless thousands of goddesses, [approached].
He went to the Tuṣita palace to the place where the World-Honored One was;
having arrived there, he prostrated himself with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One,
circumambulated him three times, and stood before the World-Honored One.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, dejected and withered, addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"That yakṣa Jvālāmukha spoke thus to the devaputra Maṇigarbha-vimala."
"In seven days from now, you will surely reach the end of your life.
What skillful means can the World-Honored One employ to enable you to practice so that you may escape this suffering?
When the World-Honored One had heard these words of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, he [responded].
Having engaged in such reflection and seen this matter,
he emitted various colored rays of light from his mouth,
which illuminated the entire trichiliocosm.
The palaces of all devas, humans, nāgas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas.
Having thus spoken,
the light returned to the place where the Buddha was,
circled him three times, and re-entered through his mouth.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Listen attentively, O Lord of Devas.
As for that son of heaven, the stainless Maṇigarbha,"
After seven days, his life will certainly come to an end;
he shall fall into hell and undergo great suffering and affliction,
with immeasurable pain and extreme terror.
Having emerged from hell, she was reborn among humans;
however, in the city of Vārāṇasī, within the household of a bamboo-worker,
she was born as a female ghost with the face of a pig in a latrine, constantly consuming excrement and urine.

Within that latrine, there were further hundreds of thousands of koṭis of maggots who constantly devoured the female spirits (yakṣiṇīs) at the three times of day until their flesh was entirely consumed and only their bones remained.
Due to the power of karma, the flesh of his body swelled up and became full once again;
having received such a body for seven full years, he then passed away and was reborn as a tortoise dwelling in a wilderness.
In that wilderness, even the name of water is not heard, let alone the water itself.
Furthermore, there are no trees and no shade;
they constantly dwell in the midday sun with bodies as if scorched, eating only hot earth.
Furthermore, his body is pecked by crows until it falls apart piece by piece;
through the power of karma, his body regrows only to split open again immediately.
Having endured such suffering for five full years, he finally passes away.
Furthermore, in that city, they are born among fish with massive bodies;
by the power of their karma, they fall into waterless places where jackals,
wolves, rats, dogs, and *niṣādaka* beasts all devour them.
Furthermore, various birds and beasts also come to devour them;
yet, by the power of their karma, they obtain water and immediately revive,
their bodies being restored once more.
Having endured such suffering for a full three years, their life comes to an end;
they are then reborn seven times among the various clans within Jambudvīpa,
where they constantly experience great misery and affliction.
Namely, the white leprosy caste,
the pukkasas caste, and the candālatarika caste.
The *ḍomba* caste, the executioner caste,
and the congenitally blind caste.
They shall undergo this evil retribution for a full sixty years.
Thereafter, they will again be born into a poor and lowly family,
with incomplete limbs and deficient wisdom.
Disregarding instructions and distancing themselves from the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha,
they are loathed by all people who see them;
they are constantly hungry and thirsty, and moreover, plagued by many illnesses.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
having heard the Buddha, the World-Honored One, speak of these various sufferings of the Maṇigarbha-vimala Devaputra,
was seized with extreme terror and fell into a state of bewildered distress.
He spoke these words: "There is no one to save us.
World-Honored One, if you do not compassionately rescue us, who then is the savior?
The World-Honored One replied: "Śakra, Lord of the Devas."
There is a dhāraṇī named "The Buddha-Crown Emission of Stainless Radiance Entering the Universal Gate to Contemplate the Hearts of All Tathāgatas.
This is a savior; it is the greatest protection against impermanence. It is difficult to seek its release from, yet even when sought, one shall obtain release.
At the time of death, in their subsequent lives and future stages, those various sentient beings will attain peace and happiness;
and those who, after death, would have fallen into any of the hells or the animal realm, shall all obtain liberation.
If one constantly maintains mindfulness, all obstacles and difficulties will be forever eliminated;
furthermore, one will attain long life, and virtuous aspirations will be fulfilled.
Moreover, one will realize the purity of intrinsic nature.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, the Four Great Kings, Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and the others,
joined their palms in reverence and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
World-Honored One, we pray that you will grant us increase and protection through the various devas.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, as a Dharma King,
may you rescue all the people of the world by the power of samādhi.
Even those in the hells and the evil destinies were all completely liberated.
World-Honored One, it was as if you were observing all sentient beings in the worlds of the four continents from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven palace.
World-Honored One, Tathāgata, you possess great wisdom.
We pray that for the sake of the world throughout the ten directions,
as well as for us, you will bestow the seal of the Dharma and grant us great protection.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, having received the earnest and repeated entreaties of those devas,
entered a samādhi called "Universal Observation of Characteristics.
When he entered that samādhi,
From within his topknot, he emitted a light of universal marks that illuminated the worlds of the ten directions everywhere;
it then remained suspended in space like a precious parasol.
At that time, the World-Honored One gazed intently at Śakra and addressed him, saying:
"Śakra, Lord of Devas, listen attentively, listen attentively!
I possess a dhāraṇī called the 'Buddhōṣṇīṣa-Emitted Stainless Radiance Entering the Universal Gate to Contemplate the Hearts of All Tathāgatas,' which is a Seal of the Dharma."
This dhāraṇī has been proclaimed by ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sands of Tathāgatas.
If there are sentient beings who...
For those who see, hear, or rejoice in this,
all their karmic offenses throughout the three periods of time that would otherwise lead to rebirth in the hells,
the evil destinies, or even as animals shall be extinguished.
All fears shall be utterly destroyed and one shall be liberated;
all karmic obstacles and transgressions shall be completely eliminated,
just as a great fire consumes dry grass.
The wind blows the ashes and embers, causing them to scatter and vanish in an instant.
Furthermore, it is like when great rain falls from heaven and its waters flow swiftly;
mountains, rivers, grasses, trees, and all manner of filth and impurities are suddenly purified.
Furthermore, just as genuine gold, when refined by fire,
becomes even more malleable before it can be fashioned into various vessels;
so too is it for one who upholds and recites this dhāraṇī.
Free from all doubt and confusion,
they see their own three karmas as pure,
like the rising sun whose radiance shines everywhere.
Furthermore, it is like a fish that has lost its water which, upon regaining the water,
dwells within it and experiences joy once more.
So too it is for all sentient beings in the world.
Those who are able to constantly recite and keep this dhāraṇī in mind will find their lifespan doubled.
Lord of Devas, listen attentively and receive this with care.

*dhūruṣka* incense, and so forth.
Take refuge and pay homage to all Tathāgatas one hundred and eight times.
I have written this Heart Sūtra and placed it within the stūpa,

Vajrapāṇi, in a past age,

by nature he was intelligent and acute, skillfully able to discern the characteristics of all phenomena.
